title: Remote blood pressure monitoring with midwife-led titration after hypertensive pregnancy: a pragmatic trial
abstract: Objective: to test whether remote blood pressure monitoring with midwife hub titration and inclusive reporting options improves blood pressure control at six weeks after a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy. Design: pragmatic trial with individual allocation. Primary outcome: blood pressure below 140 over 90 at the six-week check. Results will follow the trial.
introduction: Blood pressure often peaks after discharge, when few women are measured. Retrieved trials show that remote monitoring closes this gap and may improve six-week control, but they excluded women without smartphones.
methods: Allocation after consent on the postnatal ward; validated monitors; app, text, paper or phone reporting; titration by protocol; routine six-week measurement; intention-to-treat analysis.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present recruitment by language and digital access, reporting adherence, the primary outcome with a risk difference, and secondary outcomes.
discussion: The discussion will weigh a surrogate primary outcome against the underpowered readmission outcome and consider who the intervention reached.
limitations: Surrogate primary outcome; unblinded; single unit.
conclusion: To be written after the trial.
reportingChecklist: CONSORT extension for pragmatic trials with TIDieR
summary: CONSORT-structured draft with results left empty.
